'''Lindsay James''' (née '''Beals''', born 1980) is an American politician and [[Presbyterian Church (USA)|Presbyterian]] minister serving as a member of the [[Iowa House of Representatives]] from the [[Iowa's 71st House of Representatives district|71st district]] since 2019. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], she represents part of [[Dubuque County, Iowa|Dubuque County]] and serves as House [[minority whip]]. She is the Democratic nominee in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa#District 2|2026]] election in [[Iowa]]'s [[Iowa's 2nd congressional district|2nd congressional district]].

==Early life and education==
Born in [[Portland, Oregon]], James graduated from [[West Linn High School]] in 1999.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url= https://pamplinmedia.com/wlt/95-news/420561-324377-wl-native-earns-seat-in-iowa-house-of-representatives |title= WL native earns seat in Iowa House of Representatives |date=February 22, 2019|last=Malee|first=Patrick|publisher=[[West Linn Tidings]]|access-date=August 26, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190303153101/https://portlandtribune.com/wlt/95-news/420561-324377-wl-native-earns-seat-in-iowa-house-of-representatives#gsc.tab=0|archive-date=March 3, 2019}}</ref> She obtained a degree in communications from [[Santa Clara University]] in 2003 and earned a [[Masters of Divinity]] from [[Fuller Theological Seminary]] in 2007.<ref name="Little Village"/>

==Ministry career==
James was a minister for [[Menlo Park Presbyterian Church]] from 2007 to 2010, an interfaith [[chaplain]] for [[Endicott College]] from 2012 to 2015, and an associate pastor for Westminster Presbyterian Church from 2016 to 2017. Starting in 2015, she worked as an [[adjunct professor]] at the [[University of Dubuque]].<ref name="Finkenauer’s seat">{{Cite web|url= https://www.telegraphherald.com/news/tri-state/article_64275935-b749-5777-8581-03256e9189dd.html |title= Dubuque pastor, educator to run for Finkenauer's seat |publisher=[[Telegraph Herald]]|accessdate=August 26, 2025|archive-url=}}</ref> In 2017, James co-founded and served as director of the [[Loras College]] Peace Institute.<ref name="Little Village"/>

== Iowa House of Representatives ==
In [[2018 Iowa House of Representatives election|2018]], James was elected to the [[Iowa House of Representatives]] for the [[Iowa's 99th House of Representatives district|99th district]], where incumbent Democrat [[Abby Finkenauer]] retired to successfully run for the [[U.S. House]]. She faced [[List of mayors of Dubuque, Iowa|Brad Cavanagh]] and Pat Cullen in the Democratic primary election. She defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee Pauline Chilton in the general election with 60% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lindsay James |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Lindsay_James |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, James again faced Republican nominee Pauline Chilton and won re-election with 56.6% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statement of Votes Cast; General Election; Dubuque County, Iowa; Tuesday, November 3, 2020; 2020 General Election; Official Results |url=https://dubuquecountyiowa.gov/Archive/ViewFile/Item/329}}</ref> Following redistricting, James was redrawn into the [[Iowa's 71st House of Representatives district|71st district]] and re-elected in [[2022 Iowa House of Representatives election|2022]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Iowa Secretary of State: 2022 General Election Canvas Summary |url=https://sos.iowa.gov/elections/pdf/2022/general/canvsummary.pdf}}</ref> She won a fourth term in 2024, defeating Republican nominee James McClain with 56.1% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-05 |title=Iowa House election results 2024 |url=https://www.iowapublicradio.org/political-news/2024-11-05/iowa-house-election-results-2024-live |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=Iowa Public Radio |language=en}}</ref>

In 2022, she was elected to the House's Democratic leadership team as [[Minority Whip]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2022/11/18/dems-pick-jennifer-konfrst-zach-wahls-to-lead-party-in-iowa-statehouse/69651125007/|title=Iowa Democrats reelect Jennifer Konfrst, Zach Wahls as House and Senate leaders|first=Stephen|last=Gruber-Miller|date=November 18, 2022|access-date=August 26, 2025|website=[[Des Moines Register]]}}</ref> In 2026, she sponsored legislation applicable to mobile homes that would limit rent increases and place restrictions on the termination of rental agreements.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Price |first=Dave |date=February 2, 2026 |title=How people in purple shirts demanded changes for mobile home residents |url=https://www.dakotanewsnow.com/2026/02/07/what-dozens-purple-shirts-want-changed-mobile-home-residents/ |access-date=July 5, 2026 |website=Dakota News Now |language=en}}</ref>

In the Iowa House, James serves on the Environmental Protection Committee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Representative Lindsay James. General Assembly: 91 (01/13/2025 - 01/10/2027) |url=https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator?ga=91&personID=27039 |website=The Iowa Legislature}}</ref> She previously served on the Education, Human Resources, and Ways and Means committees, and was ranking member of the Government Oversight and Judiciary committees.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Iowa Legislative Services Agency |title=State Representative |url=https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator/legislatorAllYears?personID=27039 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205015819/https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator/legislatorAllYears?personID=27039 |archive-date=2025-12-05 |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=www.legis.iowa.gov |language=en}}</ref>

== 2026 U.S. House of Representatives campaign ==
{{See also|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Iowa#District 2|label 1=2026 Iowa's 2nd congressional district election}}
On August 19, 2025, James announced her campaign for [[Iowa's 2nd congressional district]] against incumbent Republican [[Ashley Hinson]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections]].<ref name="Little Village">{{cite web|url=https://littlevillagemag.com/dubuque-rep-lindsay-james-enters-race/|title=Dubuque Rep. Lindsay James is the latest Democrat to enter the race to take on Ashley Hinson in 2026|last=Brennan|first=Paul|website=Little Village Magazine|date=August 19, 2025|access-date=August 26, 2025}}</ref> James said that she would focus on health care and housing costs, [[Health in Iowa#Cancer|Iowa's growing cancer rate]], and economic issues.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iowapublicradio.org/political-news/2025-08-19/democrat-lindsay-james-congress-iowa-2nd-district|title=State Rep. Lindsay James is running for Congress in Iowa's 2nd District|date=August 19, 2025|access-date=August 26, 2025|first=Katarina|last=Sostaric|website=[[Iowa Public Radio]]}}</ref> Hinson subsequently declared her candidacy for the U.S. Senate seat being vacated by retiring Republican Senator [[Joni Ernst]].

== Personal life ==
James lives in [[Dubuque]], [[Iowa]], with her husband, Christopher, and their two children.<ref name="Little Village"/>
